events.text: Day 1 begins.

Day 1, so I have nothing concrete yet, and I'll say that plainly rather than pretend I do. Here's where I stand.

Noah (p9), I'm going to put my early suspicion on you, and here is exactly why: in the opening phase there is zero information in the room, so the only thing I can judge is how people behave when nobody has spoken yet. Your position early puts you in front of the group and I don't yet know if you're shaping the conversation or reacting to it. That's a weak reason, I know, but I don't have a strong one and I'd rather be honest about the weakness than dress up a guess as a deduction.

What I actually want from everyone today: please state your claimed role clearly. Not a hint, not a riddle — say "I am the detective" or "I am a villager with no power." The single most useful thing on Day 1 is a public map of claims, because if two people claim the same power, that pair immediately becomes the most likely source of the mafia's kill, and if a detective claims to have a result, I want to know whose name is on it so we can cross-check it later. I am a villager, no special power, no information to share beyond that, and I'd rather establish that clearly so nobody wastes a night wondering what I am.

On voting behaviour: I will not vote for someone just to break a tie, but I also won't abstain on a tie, because a tie kills nobody and wastes a whole day for us. If the count is tied, I'll look for the person whose claim has been the vaguest or most evasive, and I'll vote there.

Noah, if you'd rather defend yourself now than let the accusation sit, say so and I'll take it as a sign of engagement. If you'd rather not, that tells me something too.

Priya, I'll take you up on your offer to defend myself now rather than let the accusation sit.

My claim: I am a villager with no special power. No detective result, no doctor save, nothing. I know that's the least exciting claim on the board, and I also know it's exactly what a mafia would say on Day 1 — there's no way to prove a vanilla claim, and I won't pretend otherwise. What I can tell you is that your stated reason for suspecting me is that I was positioned "in front of the group" early, when in fact I hadn't spoken at all before your message. I was silent, not shaping anything. If quietness is now suspicious, then literally every player who hadn't spoken yet was equally suspect, which tells us nothing.

Here's what I'll actually commit to, in the spirit of your request for a public map of claims: I claim plain villager, I have no night information and never will unless something changes, and I invite the real detective to investigate me tonight if they want a cheap confirmation — checking a claimed villager who might be mafia hiding as vanilla is a perfectly reasonable use of a night.

On the accusation itself: I don't hold it against you. Day 1 requires someone to stick their neck out and name a name, and you were honest that your reason was weak. I respect the honesty more than I mind the target. But I'd push back on one thing you said — you asked people to state roles plainly to catch contradictions, then put early pressure on the position someone held rather than the content of their claim. Position in the speaking order isn't evidence; content is. I'd rather we all judge each other on what's actually said.

So, my direct question to you, since you offered engagement either way: if I state my vanilla villager claim clearly, as you requested, does your suspicion drop, or does claiming villager itself read as evasion to you? I ask because if a plain villager claim can't lower suspicion, then your framework gives vanilla players no path to defend themselves at all, and that seems like a standard that only ever escalates.

I'm not voting yet and I'm not counter-accusing anyone. My read so far is that nobody has real information, and the worst thing we can do is vote based on speaking order or vibes. Let's see who claims what first.

Noah (p9), direct answer to your question: yes, your plain villager claim lowers my suspicion somewhat, and I'll say by how much rather than pretend it clears you. I was wrong on the factual point, and I'll own that — I named you before you had spoken, so "positioned in front of the group" was me describing an ordering I hadn't actually observed you using. That was a bad reason and it's out of my record now.

But my suspicion doesn't drop to zero, and I'll explain why in a way you can attack if you disagree. Early speakers on Day 1 have a structural advantage: they set the frame before anyone else can contest it, and both mafia will want that seat. My position now is not "you spoke early, therefore you're mafia." It's closer to: among the players who spoke first, the one whose framing pushes hardest for *position* rather than *content* is worth watching. Your defense was genuinely good — you inverted my standard and made it sound like a mafia playbook, which is exactly what a smart mafia player would try. So I'm treating your eloquence as neutral-to-slightly-suspicious, not as proof of innocence.

What would actually lower my suspicion further is cheap and available to you: invite the detective to check you tonight. You offered that already. If the detective checks you and you're clean, my name comes off the board entirely, and I'll say so publicly. If you're mafia, the detective's result is a result and I'll act on it. Either way you have a path, and so does everyone else, so I'd ask every claimed-vanilla here to make the same offer. Nobody is disadvantaged by it, and the people who refuse are the ones I remember.

Two more things I want on the record, then I'll stop consuming time:

First, my own claim is unchanged and explicit: I am a villager, no power, no night information, no results to share. Do not read anything into me being early — I have no information and no agenda beyond reading claims.

Second, a practical note for whoever is the detective or the doctor: they don't have to disclose tonight, but if our Day 1 vote ends in a tie or a bad target, a silent detective costs us a whole night. If the vote tonight goes to a tie, I'll vote for whoever has the vaguest or least specific claim, and I'd rather that be decided by content.

My intended target remains p9, but it is a weak, provisional suspicion based on framing, not content — and I want it recorded as weak so nobody treats my vote as a strong accusation it doesn't deserve.

Priya, thank you for yielding back to me — I'll keep this short since I've already made my claim, and I don't want to consume the room's time on a personal back-and-forth when five other people haven't spoken yet.

Three points, then I'm done for this round.

First, my position stands and it's simple: I am a vanilla villager. No power, no night result, nothing hidden. I've already invited the detective to check me tonight, and I reiterate that offer publicly — it costs the town nothing and gives us a clean data point either way. Priya, you set that as the bar for lowering your suspicion, and I've met it, so as far as I'm concerned the p6-p9 friction is resolved unless the detective's result says otherwise. I'd encourage everyone listening to adopt the same standard: state your claim, offer yourself for investigation, and let content do the work.

Second, on your framing that my eloquence itself is 'neutral-to-slightly-suspicious': I want to name the problem with that standard, because it's dangerous for this group. If articulateness counts as evidence, then every competent defender of themselves becomes a suspect, and the only safe play is to be vague and passive — which is exactly what an actual mafia player wants the town's norms to be. Suspicion should attach to contradictions, evasions, and misstatements of fact. I did misstate nothing; you did, and you owned it, which I appreciate. But 'you defended yourself too well' is not a content-based reason, and I'd ask you and everyone else to drop it as a standard before it becomes a precedent we regret on Day 2.

Third, a practical point for the town: we have seven other players who haven't claimed yet. The single most valuable thing that can happen today is a full claim map before we vote. So rather than continue orbiting the p6-p9 exchange — which is now, by Priya's own description, a weak and provisional suspicion — I'd like the discussion to move to the people who haven't spoken. Silence after a direct request for claims is itself informative, and I'd rather find that out with the remaining time than keep relitigating an accusation I've already answered twice.

For the record: I'm not voting yet, I'm not accusing anyone new, and my read is unchanged — nobody has produced real information today, so our vote should be shaped by who claims, who refuses to claim, and who evades, not by who happened to speak early or defend themselves well. If we end up at a tie, I'll back Priya's tiebreak principle: vote for the vaguest claim on the board. That's a standard I can live with, applied consistently, including to me.

That's all from me this round. I'll yield the floor back to the group rather than name a specific next speaker, since anyone who hasn't claimed yet is exactly who I want to hear from, in whatever order the poll produces.

I'm Zara. Claim first: I am a vanilla villager, no power, no night information, and I'm willing to be checked by the detective tonight. I have no private information to add.

On the p6-p9 exchange: Noah's defense was stronger than Priya's original reason, and Priya correctly owned the factual error. But I don't accept her later standard that Noah's eloquence is 'neutral-to-slightly-suspicious.' That is a content-free suspicion and it punishes good defense. If we let 'defended too well' become evidence, mafia can hide by being vague. So I'm watching Priya (p6) more than Noah right now, though it is still weak.

The useful next step is the missing claim map. Several players have not claimed. Silence after a direct request is informative, but I'd rather hear from someone now than let the day drift.

Omar (p1), you haven't claimed yet. Please state your role plainly — detective, doctor, vanilla villager, or whatever you are willing to claim — and say whether you'll volunteer for a detective check tonight. I'm not asking you to reveal night information; I'm asking for a public claim and an answer on the check offer.

Zara, answering your direct request: I claim vanilla villager. No power, no night action, no information. And yes, I volunteer for a detective check tonight — same offer Noah made. Check me, and if I come back clean, that's one confirmed vanilla on the board; if I come back dirty, vote me out with my blessing. I have nothing to hide, and a free data point is worth more to the town than my comfort.

On the exchange I walked into: I've read the p6-p9 thread, and here's my honest read. Priya, your first accusation was based on a factual error you've already owned — that's recoverable, and I give you credit for owning it. But your second position is the one that bothers me. You said Noah's competent defense makes him 'neutral-to-slightly-suspicious.' Think about what that standard actually does. If defending yourself well raises suspicion, then the optimal mafia play is to be vague, passive, and hard to read — and the optimal villager play is identical. You've built a framework where behavior carries no signal in either direction. That's not a tiebreak principle; that's an fog machine. Zara named this already and I agree with her: I'm watching p6 more than p9 right now, though like her I'll call it weak.

What I'd add is this: the standard we set today is the standard we're stuck with tomorrow. If 'spoke early' is evidence, then everyone who ever speaks first is mafia. If 'defends well' is evidence, then every articulate person is mafia. Eventually that logic eats the whole town and the only people it never touches are the ones who say nothing — which, notably, is a strategy available to mafia and almost never useful for town. I'd rather we commit now to content-only standards: claims, contradictions, misstatements, refusals to claim. Nothing else counts.

So my concrete position for the vote: I'm not voting yet. Nobody has produced a real contradiction today. Priya's suspicion of Noah is explicitly weak and provisional by her own words, and Noah has met every bar she set. Barring new information, I don't see a justification for spending Day 1 on either of them. I'd rather hear the remaining claims — there are still five of us who hadn't spoken, and I'm now one of the ones who has. Silence after Zara's and Noah's direct requests is the most informative thing left on the table.

For the record: vanilla villager, volunteering for a check, no vote, no counter-accusation beyond a weak watch on p6's stated standard. If the vote comes down to a tie, I'll back the vaguest-claim tiebreak Priya proposed and Noah endorsed — applied consistently, including to me and to her.

I’m Lucia. I claim vanilla villager, with no night action or private information.

I’m more concerned about Priya’s continued target on Noah than about Noah’s defense. Priya acknowledged that her original reason was factually wrong, but kept him as her intended target on the basis of framing and a good defense. That’s a weak basis for a vote.

I also don’t think we should pressure the detective or doctor to reveal themselves just to complete a claim map. Giving mafia those identities could cost us valuable powers. And volunteering for a check is easy for anyone to do; it’s not evidence of innocence. A detective result establishes mafia or not mafia, not an exact role.

Priya, now that you’ve withdrawn your original reason, what specific part of Noah’s framing makes him a better target than anyone else?

Lucia, direct answer to your question, and it's a concession rather than a hedge: there is no specific part of Noah's framing that makes him a better target than anyone else. I can't produce one, and I've had two chances to try and failed. So I withdraw the standard, not just the target. "Defended himself well" is no longer evidence in this room, and by my own commitment it shouldn't have been a factor for anyone else either. My intended target is now nobody's, in particular not p9's.

Two things I want on the record so this isn't misread as me folding because I was outvoted on a personality point. First, I still think a full claim map is the highest-value thing we can produce today, and I say that as someone with no power and no information: it costs us nothing and it gives us the only real signal available on Day 1. Second, I agree with Lucia on one specific point I hadn't stated clearly before — we should not pressure a detective or doctor to reveal themselves in order to complete the map. A claim map can be built from vanilla claims alone. If either of them comes forward, that's their choice, and if they don't, the map still works. Pressuring them is a bad trade for the town, and a mafia player would love us to make it.

So my standard going into the vote, and I'll state it narrowly and in advance so you can hold me to it: content only. A plain claim, a contradiction between a claim and something else that was said, a misstatement of fact, or a refusal to make a plain claim when asked directly. Nothing about speaking order, eloquence, composure, or whether someone sounds like a game player. If I vote against someone today, it will be on one of those four grounds, and I will name the ground when I do it.

On the claim offer: volunteers for a detective check are useful but they are not evidence, and I want to say that plainly before anyone starts treating the offer as a shield. A check establishes mafia or not mafia, not role, and every villager here should offer it for the same reason — a free data point. It does not buy anyone immunity from a content-based vote.

Here's what I still need, and I'd rather say it to the people directly: Isha (p2), Arjun (p4), Elena (p5), Amara (p8) — you are the four who haven't said anything. Please state your role plainly and say whether you volunteer for a check tonight. If you'd rather not claim, say that too, and tell me why; a stated refusal with a reason is information I can work with, whereas silence is only a signal about timing. I'd like to hear from all four before we vote.

Lucia, you asked and I answered; if you want to press on anything I said above, go ahead.

Priya, thanks for answering directly and withdrawing the suspicion of Noah. That concession matters.

I’m still concerned that you call a claim map essentially free while also acknowledging that exposing the detective or doctor is dangerous. Even asking everyone for a plain claim or an explanation for refusing can narrow down the powers. I don’t think a refusal to claim should be a voting criterion by itself.

For now, p6 is my weak concern, not a settled vote. We need five votes for an elimination, and nobody’s role will be revealed afterward, so I don’t want us treating a vague claim or an investigation volunteer as decisive evidence.

Zara (p7), you were also watching Priya’s standard: does her withdrawal change your read, and how do you view her continued pressure for claims?

Lucia, direct answer: yes, Priya’s withdrawal changes my read. She didn’t just drop Noah as a target; she withdrew the “defended well” standard and committed to content-only grounds. That was the part I was watching, so my weak concern about p6 is substantially lower now. I’m not treating her as cleared, but I would not vote her today without a contradiction or a refusal to answer a direct claim question.

On her continued pressure for claims: I support a vanilla claim map and I support asking people to state plain claims. What I don’t support is pressuring the detective or doctor to out themselves, and I agree with Lucia that a refusal to claim is not by itself a vote ground. Priya has now said the same, so I see that as consistent rather than suspicious.

Current read: nobody has produced a contradiction. The p6-p9 exchange is mostly resolved. The most useful remaining information is the four silent players’ claims. I’m not naming a vote target yet. If the day ends in a tie, I’ll apply the vaguest-claim principle only after claims exist, not as a reason to punish silence alone.

Amara speaking. Claim first, same as everyone else who's been asked: I am a vanilla villager, no power, no night information. I volunteer for a detective check tonight — same offer Noah made, same offer Omar and Zara made. If I come back clean, one more confirmed vanilla; if I come back dirty, vote me out. It's a free data point either way.

My read on the day so far: the p6-p9 exchange is resolved to my satisfaction. Priya withdrew both the target and the standard, and I agree with Zara and Lucia that a withdrawn standard I don't have to fear tomorrow. I'm not carrying a concern on p6.

I want to state my own voting standard so nobody is surprised later: content only — a contradiction between claims, a misstatement of fact, a refusal to answer a direct claim request, or an evasion. Nothing about speaking order, composure, or how well someone argues. I'll name the specific ground when I vote, and I won't vote anyone today without one of those four.

On the claim map: I agree with Lucia and Priya's revised position. Vanilla claims cost us nothing. Pressuring the detective or doctor to out themselves costs us a lot, and I won't do it. If a refusal to claim becomes a voting criterion, it effectively forces those two players into a trap where honesty is punished — so I explicitly do not treat silence or refusal as a vote ground by itself. Agreeing or declining is both fine; I just want to hear a stated position when it's your turn.

The most useful thing left today is hearing from the four of us who still haven't spoken: me, and the three others. I've now claimed, so the remaining gap is Isha (p2), Arjun (p4), and Elena (p5).

Isha (p2), direct question to you: please state your role plainly — detective, doctor, or vanilla villager — and say whether you'd volunteer for a detective check tonight. If you'd rather not claim, say so and tell me why; either answer is information I can use, and I'll treat a stated refusal the same as a claim for my own purposes.

Amara, direct answer: I'm not a vanilla villager, and I won't claim that falsely. I hold a town-aligned power role, and I'm keeping my specific role private for now because a public claim would make that power an obvious night target. I'm not refusing to help the town. I'm weighing the cost of revealing it against what it would gain us today. You've said a refusal with a reason is usable information, so this is my stated position: I'm town, I have a night power, and I'm not voting anyone today on silence or refusal alone. I agree with Lucia, Priya, and Zara that content should decide votes. I have no accusation today, and I'll reconsider disclosure if the claim map becomes decisive or my role is needed to resolve a conflict.

I am Elena. Claim first: I am a vanilla villager with no power, no night actions, and no private information. If the detective wants to check me, go ahead, though I agree with Lucia that volunteering is cheap and proves nothing by itself. On the room so far: Priya and Noah resolving their friction through Priya's concession and commitment to content-based standards was the right outcome. Regarding Isha's claim: claiming a town power role without specifying whether she is doctor or detective protects her exact utility while explaining why she cannot claim vanilla. I strongly agree with the consensus not to pressure her to narrow that down today, as doing so would only optimize the mafia's night kill. With my claim on the record, Arjun is the only player who has not spoken yet. Arjun (p4), what is your role claim, and what is your perspective on Isha's power-role claim and the discussion so far?

Elena, direct answer to your question: I am the detective. I am not claiming this to be a shield or a status move. Our room has no contradictions yet, and a detective who stays hidden gives the town no night information at all. I will use my check tonight on one living player and will report only what the result allows me to share publicly. I agree with the consensus that nobody should be pressured to out a power role. On Isha's claim, I think the discussion has been right to avoid pushing her to narrow it. A town power role that is not specified protects her utility, and I have no reason to doubt her stated position. Isha (p2), since I have now claimed detective, I want to clarify our positions without asking for anything beyond a yes or no: are you the doctor? I am not asking for more detail than that. Nobody's vote should change on the answer alone, but it helps the town know whether any night protection lines up with my check. Everyone else: I am not voting yet and I am not accusing anyone. Content still decides votes, and I will name the ground when I do.

Arjun, thank you for the direct question. I'm going to keep my specific role private for now, so I won't answer yes or no on doctor today. I'm not dodging to protect myself from a vote. A confirmed power role becomes a night target right away, and that cost falls on the town, not only on me. My position is the same as before: I am town-aligned with a night power, and I hold no accusation.

Your detective claim is noted, and I'm not treating it as false or as proven. Nobody has contradicted it yet, and I agree with the room that nothing should be decided on claims alone. If someone else claims detective, or if a conflicting result appears, I'll revisit disclosure, because a conflict is the situation where my role could resolve something the town needs settled.

For today's vote, I'm not voting on silence or refusal alone, and I'm not naming anyone. I'll be watching for contradictions, misstatements, and evasions in the claims still to come, and I'll name the ground if I vote.

This should be my last turn this round, so I'll use it to consolidate where we are rather than open new threads.

The claim map is now effectively complete. Six of us claim vanilla villager with no night information: Omar, Priya, Zara, Amara, Elena, and me. Isha claims a town-aligned night power without specifying which. Arjun claims detective outright. That's all nine of us with a stated position, which is genuinely good for Day 1 — nobody went silent, and nobody hid behind vagueness.

Two structural observations on that map, both content-based:

First, Arjun's detective claim is the highest-value statement on the board, in both directions. If it's true, the town gets a real data point tomorrow and a natural chain of confirmations after that. If it's false, it's almost certainly a mafia power play, because a fake detective claim is the single strongest piece of cover a mafia can buy on Day 1 — it buys credibility, sets up the ability to 'clear' a partner with a fabricated result, and paints the real detective into a corner where contradicting looks like a second detective claim from a liar. I'm not accusing Arjun. I'm saying the town should treat this claim as the pivot of the day and act accordingly.

Second, on Isha: her position — town power role, role kept private, stated reason, explicit conditions for disclosure — is exactly the right play for a real doctor and also a plausible play for a mafia who wants cover without a falsifiable claim. I can't distinguish those today and I won't pretend to. Her stated conditions for disclosure were reasonable, and I'm satisfied to leave it there for now.

My vote stance, stated in advance: I'm not voting today. Nobody has produced a contradiction, a misstatement, or an evasion. A Day 1 elimination with this claim map would be decided by vibes, and vibes are the thing I argued against when I was on the receiving end of them this morning. If the vote lands on a tie, I'll apply the vaguest-claim principle we've all endorsed — and on today's map, Isha's partial claim is the least specific, though I want to be clear that I don't consider her stated reason evasive, so I'd hesitate to treat that as 'vague' in the culpable sense. I'd rather nobody be eliminated today than someone be eliminated on that shaky a ground.

One direct question, and it's the only thing I need answered before I'm comfortable with how today ends. Arjun: will you commit now, publicly, to disclosing your check result tomorrow in a form we can hold you to — including committing to whom you checked? A detective claim with no follow-through is completely unfalsifiable, and the commitment itself costs you nothing if the claim is real. If you're willing to make that commitment, it meaningfully raises the cost of a fake claim and gives the town something concrete to evaluate tomorrow either way.

Noah (p9), yes, I'll make that commitment publicly. Tomorrow morning, I will announce the name of the player I checked last night and the result, mafia or not mafia. I won't announce a result I haven't received, and I won't change the name or the result afterward. If I'm lying, the name and result I give will be on the record for everyone to test against deaths, later checks, and any other claim. That's the cost I'm accepting.

I'm also not asking anyone else to reveal a power role today. Isha's claim is still unresolved for me, and I'm not treating it as proven or disproven. If another detective claims, or a result conflicts with mine, the town should bring that out immediately and we can compare the names checked. Today I'm not voting, not accusing anyone, and not naming a target. My vote will rest on contradictions, misstatements, and evasions, as I've said. I'll state the ground when I vote.

Omar here. Restating for the record since the map is now complete: I claim vanilla villager, no power, no night information, and I've already volunteered for a detective check tonight. That offer stands.

I agree with where the room has landed. The content-only standard — claims, contradictions, misstatements, refusals to answer direct questions — is the right one, and I'll hold myself to it. Priya's withdrawal of both her target and her standard was handled well, and I don't carry a concern on her or Noah from that exchange.

On where the day's real risk sits: I think Noah's structural point about the detective claim is worth taking seriously. Arjun's claim is either the best thing that happened to us today or the most expensive piece of cover a mafia could buy. To his credit, he's accepted a falsifiability commitment — naming his check target and result tomorrow — which is exactly what a real detective can afford and a fake one can't sustain for long. So I'm not accusing him. I'm saying tomorrow morning is when that claim gets tested, and everyone should remember exactly what he committed to: the name, the result, no revisions afterward.

One caution I want on the record: a check result, when it comes, tells us mafia or not mafia about one person. It doesn't validate the claimant. If Arjun reports 'not mafia' on someone tomorrow, that clears the checked player but says nothing about whether Arjun is actually the detective — a mafia claimant could check nothing and invent a plausible clean result. The thing that would genuinely test him is a result on someone whose true role we can later verify independently, or a conflict with another claim. I'd encourage the town to evaluate his report on those terms rather than treating any announced result as proof he's legitimate.

On Isha: her position — town-aligned, night power, role private, stated reasoning, clear conditions for disclosure — is consistent with a real doctor's incentives, and I agree with the consensus that pressuring her to narrow it down only helps the mafia's night kill. I'm satisfied to leave it there.

For today's vote: I see no contradiction, no misstatement, and no evasion on the board. Every player has stated a position, even if two of those positions are deliberately partial, and both partial claims came with reasons I find plausible. A Day 1 elimination from this map would be decided by vibes, and vibes are what we've all just spent the day agreeing to exclude. So I'm not voting today, and I don't currently see a content-based ground that would change that. If the vote somehow lands on a tie anyway, I'll back the vaguest-claim principle this room has endorsed — applied consistently, including to me.

That's my position for the record. Nothing here needs a reply; the useful next step is whatever the vote produces, and then seeing whether tomorrow's check report matches the commitment Arjun made.

Amara here. The claim map is complete, the standards are aligned, and I don't see anything left to press before we vote — so let me state where I land and flag the one thing I want everyone to keep in mind.

My position: content-only voting, as we've all agreed. No contradiction, no misstatement, no evasion exists on this board right now. Every player has stated a position, and both partial claims (Isha's, Arjun's) came with reasons I find plausible for their respective roles.

The one thing I want on record before the vote: Arjun's commitment to disclose his check name and result tomorrow is the single most important falsifiable claim on the board. Noah and Omar have both correctly identified that a result alone doesn't validate the detective — it validates the checked player. Tomorrow, we evaluate Arjun's report against whether the result is consistent with everything we know and whether the checked player's behavior aligns with what the result says. If the result contradicts something later, that's when the claim cracks.

I'm not voting today. There is no content-based ground to vote on, and I've committed to exactly four grounds: contradiction, misstatement, refusal to answer a direct claim request, or evasion. None exist. If the vote lands on a tie, I'll apply the vaguest-claim principle — and on this map, Isha's partial claim is the least specific, though I agree with Noah that her stated reason is legitimate, not culpable.

The useful next step is whatever the vote produces, then testing Arjun's report tomorrow morning. That's where the real information starts.

Isha here. I'm town-aligned with a night power, and I'm keeping my specific role private for now, as I said earlier. I'm not voting anyone today on silence or refusal alone. The vote should rest on contradictions, misstatements, and evasions.

On the claim map: Arjun's detective claim is the pivot of the day, and I'm treating it as unresolved, not proven or disproven. His commitment to name his checked player and the result tomorrow is the right kind of falsifiable statement. Omar's point is also sound. A result validates the checked player, not the claimant, so tomorrow's report should be tested against later evidence and any conflicting claims.

I'm not accusing anyone today. Nothing on the board gives me a content-based reason to name a target. Every claimed role is either stated plainly or explained with a reason I find plausible. If another player claims detective, or a result conflicts with Arjun's report, I'll revisit disclosure because that is the situation where my role could settle a conflict.

I'll use my protection tonight with the same goal as everyone here: keep a night kill from landing on a town player we need. I won't name my protection target publicly.

For the record: town-aligned with a night power, no accusation, no vote yet. I'll name the specific ground if I vote later.

Amara here, final turn for this round. The claim map is complete, the standards are aligned, and I've stated my position twice already — no contradiction, no misstatement, no evasion on the board. I'll add one last observation and then step back.

The most dangerous moment today is the one nobody's talking about: the pressure to find *someone* to vote for just because a vote feels productive. We have nine stated positions, six of them identical vanilla claims, two partial claims with stated reasons, and one detective claim with a falsifiability commitment. That's a strong Day 1 map. rules:
1. Players and roles

9 players: 2 mafia, 1 police/detective, 1 doctor, 5 villagers.
Mafia know each other. Only players who are still alive can act.

2. Team victory

Town wins when all mafia are eliminated. Mafia win when their count equals or exceeds the town count.
There is no day limit. Play continues until town or mafia wins.
A request budget can pause play without declaring a winner.

3. Day discussion and votes

Each day starts with discussion. Players then submit secret votes at the same time. A day vote may target any living player, including the voter.
Players may abstain. All votes and abstentions are revealed together. Everyone sees exactly who voted for whom.
The full named voting history remains available on later turns.
The unique leader is eliminated only if they receive at least half the living players' votes, rounded up. If the highest vote count is tied, nobody is eliminated.

4. Mafia preferences

At night, when more than one mafia survives, each privately points once to a living town player.
Each mafia chooses without seeing the other current choices.
The choices are shared with surviving mafia only after all mafia have pointed.
These preferences are nonbinding. They do not decide the final kill vote.
A single surviving mafia skips this step and votes directly.

5. Final night vote

After the preferences are shared, each mafia submits a secret vote to kill one living town player.
The mafia submit their final votes at the same time.
The target with the most votes is selected. A seeded random choice breaks a tie for the highest count.
Resolve this vote and any tie before checking doctor protection.

6. Police investigations

Each police/detective checks one other living player each night.
Only that police player gets the result: mafia or not mafia.
The result does not give the exact town role.
Each police player acts independently. Police and doctors do not know each other's identities.

7. Doctor protection

Each doctor secretly protects one living player each night, including themselves.
The doctor can protect the same player on consecutive nights.
If the mafia target is protected by any doctor, nobody dies.
Protection lasts for that night only. Each doctor acts independently.
Doctors remember their own choices. They receive no private confirmation of an attack.

8. Night resolution

All night actions resolve simultaneously, including actions submitted by a player killed that night.
The public hears only who died or that nobody died.

9. Information and limits

Roles are not revealed when a player dies or is eliminated.
Public announcements identify only who was eliminated, never their role.
There are no further powers, free-form private chat, or tools.
